tasks.title: Design fresh desktop and terminal pixel-character workspaces
tasks.description: Produce paired desktop and terminal design studies for a new pixel-character workspace, including session characters, task/phase stations, dependency/routing views and selected evidence. Define layout, character identity, pixel art rules, typography, state/mode labels, static/text fallbacks and fresh asset locations without reusing current RPG or older city/pigeon art. Default links are expressed by one character walking to another and playing an interaction; shared stations/props are optional. Specify clip poses and foot/facing anchors for that sequence.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewable desktop and terminal studies show the same project/session/task identity and evidence across different layouts.
Desktop composition is newly designed; current RPG/city/pigeon art is not reused or listed as fallback material.
Running, review, failure, stale contact, replay, simulation, reduced motion, missing art and ASCII-only terminal cases are shown.
Readable evidence/controls and compact 80x24 terminal behavior are specified; characters/stations do not introduce new execution logic.

tasks.title: Prototype Rust actor movement and sprite playback
tasks.description: Prototype one character approaching another, facing the target, playing an interaction clip and settling using a fresh registered test atlas. Compare a small hand-built Rust clip/sequence runtime with a reusable animation library. Document the selected playback boundary, frame/anchor/timing metadata, presentation state and drawing integration; do not dispatch agents or change workflow lifecycles.
acceptance_criteria: One actor walks to another and plays a two-character interaction with stable foot anchors, facing and offsets; a shared station is optional.
Rust presentation state/frame sampling is independent of execution and the drawing backend; Tauri/webview versus a Rust-rendered surface is assessed explicitly.
Replay seeks, new events, cancellation, stale contact and reduced motion settle/reconstruct the scene without stale movement queues or delayed workflow outcomes.

A representative prototype records the hand-built versus library tradeoff, native Windows/Linux support, asset requirements and terminal cell/text equivalent; no game-framework commitment without evidence.
